questions.q: What does DBUA (Database Upgrade Assistant) do?
options: Upgrades an existing database in place to a newer Oracle version, using the same data files under newer software
Automatically converts an Oracle database into a different database platform
Only works for migrating between different operating systems
Exports all data to a dump file for import into a new database
questions.explain: DBUA performs an in-place upgrade, running catalog upgrade scripts against the existing database rather than moving data to a new one.

questions.q: What is AutoUpgrade's relationship to DBUA?
options: It's Oracle's more recently recommended, script-driven successor for the same in-place upgrade path, with better fleet-upgrade support
AutoUpgrade is only used for Data Pump exports, unrelated to upgrades
AutoUpgrade and DBUA perform completely unrelated operations
AutoUpgrade replaced DBUA entirely and DBUA no longer exists
questions.explain: AutoUpgrade automates the same in-place upgrade path as DBUA with better batch/fleet support, though DBUA remains real and still in active use.

questions.q: When is Data Pump export/import migration the better strategy over an in-place upgrade?
options: Only when no pre-upgrade checks are available
Only for databases under 1 GB in size
When the destination is genuinely different — new hardware, a different operating system, consolidation, or too large a version jump for in-place
It is always strictly worse than DBUA in every scenario
questions.explain: Data Pump migration is more flexible across platform and version boundaries, at the cost of being slower for large databases since data is unloaded and reloaded.

questions.q: What does Oracle's Pre-Upgrade Information Tool (preupgrade.jar) do?
options: Is only relevant to RAC clusters, not single-instance databases
Automatically fixes every possible upgrade issue with no DBA involvement
Flags upgrade blockers on the source database, such as deprecated features, invalid objects, and parameter changes, before the upgrade begins
Performs the actual data export for a Data Pump migration
questions.explain: The tool surfaces version-specific blockers ahead of time so they can be addressed deliberately instead of causing a mid-upgrade outage.

questions.q: A company is moving to new hardware with a different operating system, three major versions newer than their current Oracle database. Which strategy fits better?
options: AutoUpgrade must be used exclusively for any cross-platform move
Data Pump migration, because it works across different operating systems and larger version gaps that an in-place tool may not support directly
DBUA in-place upgrade, because it works identically regardless of hardware or OS changes
Neither strategy can handle an operating system change; the data must be re-entered manually
questions.explain: A platform (OS/hardware) change is exactly the scenario where Data Pump migration into a freshly created target database is the appropriate, flexible approach.
